english.title: Breach Article 41(1) by transporting waste destined for disposal that has come from unspecified third country / area
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) in breach Article 41(1) of Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council on shipments of waste, transported waste, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE OF THE WASTE..), destined for disposal that had come from

(A)_[a third country,]_
(B)_[an area,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THE COUNTRY / AREA..), which was not specified in that Article
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 26 and 58 of the Transfrontier Shipment of Waste Regulations 2007.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location,
in breach of Article 41(1) of Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006,
transport waste destined for disposal that has come from a third country or area
other than those specified in that Article

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
